title: FACS protocol for direct comparison of cell populations isolated from mice
protocol: Weigh and randomize 4–5 females in cages with clean bedding for 2 days prior to step 1b.
Transfer one tablespoon of urine-saturated bedding from the corner of a male cage primarily used as a toilet to the middle of the female cage.
Begin analysis of vaginal cytology in the morning 24–36 hours after adding the male bedding.
Restrain the mouse by scruffing the skin on the dorsal side between the shoulders.
Rotate your wrist with the mouse in a supine ventral posterior position.
Lavage the vagina using 10 μL of sterile PBS twice.
Collect the third flush containing the vaginal cells into a labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Remove any excreted urine on the animal’s belly using a sterile dry towel.
Place the pipet tip against the vulva and eject liquid to wash out the vagina.
Flushes should be collected at the same time each day.
Analyze the vaginal cytology based on the ratio of cell types.
Spray the ventral surface of the euthanized mouse with 70% ethanol and wipe with gauze.
Create a Y-shaped incision along the ventral side from the bottom of the abdomen toward the thorax, and additional incisions radiating towards each limb.
Separate skin fascia from the abdominal wall using forceps and scissors to expose mammary fat pads.
Remove mouse mammary fat pads carefully without piercing the peritoneal cavity.
Remove surrounding tissue from the mammary fat pad, including hair and extraneous tissue.
Remove the thin layer of muscle overlying thoracic glands 2 and 3.
Remove the lymph node in gland number 4.
Pinch each fat pad with forceps and gently pull away from skin.
Separate the gland from the underlying connective tissue using scissors.
Focus initially on the edge of the fat pad when separating.
Prepare mammary fat pad pairs 2 and 3, and 4 and 5 together for removal.
Place removed tissue in formalin for 48 hours followed by transfer to 70% ethanol at 4°C for long-term storage.
Dehydrate and embed tissue after storing in ethanol for downstream analysis purposes.
Place the glands of one mouse in 6–10 mL of premade freezing media for cryopreservation.
Store cryopreserved samples at -80°C for short term use (less than 1 month).
Transfer cryopreserved samples to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage (more than 1 month).
Rapidly thaw cryopreserved samples at 37°C with gentle swirling until the medium is liquid.
Place the excised mammary glands in a 6 cm dish with 1 mL DMEM/F12.
Chop the glands finely using scissors or a scalpel until they resemble a homogenous sludge with no large tissue pieces.
Transfer the homogenized tissue into a 50 mL conical tube containing 14 mL of pre-warmed digestion media.
Place the tube in the incubator at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Keep the tube cap on loosely to allow for gas exchange.
Incubate and mix the tissue manually as needed based on available time and labor resources.
Monitor fibrous material during the digestion process.
Remove fibers using a P20 pipette with as little liquid as possible when they first appear.
Pellet digested material at 150 × g for 5 min.
Gently aspirate the supernatant, avoiding complete removal of liquid.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of DNase I solution and incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 3–5 min.
Manually remove any remaining large fibers if necessary.
Add 500 μL of FBS to the cell suspension after digestion is complete.
Mix gently and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Pellet cell suspension at 150 × g for 10 min.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of PBS by gentle pipetting up and down ∼10–20 times using a P1000 pipet.
Add 9 mL of PBS.
Pellet at 350 × g for 20 seconds.
Repeat steps 5b, v, and vi twice using a 10 mL serological pipet instead of a P1000 to keep the cells as clusters so they spin down efficiently.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of PBS after each wash step.
Remove 10 μL of the cell suspension and place it as a single drop on a glass slide.
Observe under a microscope.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of Accumax by gently pipetting 20 times using a P1000 pipet.
Bring up the Accumax volume to 3 mL.
Divide the sample equally into three 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Incubate in a Thermomixer at 37°C for 10 minutes at 800 rpm.
Pipette the suspension with a P200 every two minutes during incubation.
Remove large fibrous aggregates using a P200 as described.
Remove the tubes from the Thermomixer.
Pellet the cells at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Recombine samples using 0.5 mL Trypsin solution.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 3–5 minutes.
Determine the proportion of single cells by microscopic observation.
Add 0.5 mL of FBS to quench the trypsin.
Gently mix by pipetting.
Pellet the cells at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of PBS by gentle pipetting up and down ∼10–20 times using a P1000 pipet.
Take up the suspension into a 1 mL syringe.
Pass the cell suspension through a 70 μm mesh into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Mix 70% ethanol with nylon mesh to sterilize.
Dry nylon mesh after soaking in 70% ethanol.
Cut the end of a plastic syringe cap and clamp the nylon mesh to the syringe using the cap.
Discard the syringe needle.
Take a 10 μL aliquot of filtered cell suspension and count cells using a hemocytometer.
Place cell suspension on ice until further processing is required.
Optimize antibody and dye titration for FACS analysis, timing approximately 4 hours for one antibody staining.
Perform additional 2-4 hours for FACS analysis after initial optimization.
Include viability dye Zombie Yellow first in the optimization process.
Stain cells with the optimized viability dye Zombie Yellow.
Transfer 1 × 10^5 cells into each of five 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes labeled as indicated.
Adjust volume to 50 μL if necessary.
Add dyes at the calculated concentrations.
Incubate at 21°C–23°C in the dark for 20–30 min.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each tube and centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend in 1 mL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend in 250 μL to 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Store on wet ice in the dark until ready to analyze.
Resuspend cells in PBS supplemented with 0.5%–1% BSA.
Transfer 1 × 10^5 cells into each of five 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Block by adding 0.5 μg of IgG to the cells.
Incubate at 21°C–23°C for 10 minutes.
Add conjugated primary antibody at calculated concentrations.
Incubate on wet ice in the dark for 20–30 minutes.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each tube and centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 250 μL to 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Titrate antibody and dye concentrations according to the prior protocol before proceeding.
Combine cells across cell preparations from all animals being analyzed for controls.
Use combined cells for compensation controls in subsequent steps.
Aliquot approximately 1 × 10^5 cells in PBS into each of 12 microfuge tubes and adjust the volume to 150 μL if necessary.
Label the control tubes 1 through 12 for compensation controls.
Alquot approximately 2 × 10^6 cells from each genotype into two microfuge tubes and adjust the volume to 150 μL if necessary.
Label experimental tubes: tube #13 as 13-G1_1, tube #14 as 14-G1_2, tube #15 as 15-G2_1, and tube #16 as 16-G2_2.
Add ZY to tubes 2, 4, and 10–16.
Add CTV to tubes 5, 10–13, and 15.
Mix the tubes by gently flicking them with your finger.
Incubate the tubes at 21°C–23°C for 20–30 minutes.
Add 1,350 μL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge the tubes at 350 × g for 5 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant from the tubes.
Resuspend cells in tubes 1–12 in 150 μL of FACS buffer and tubes 13–16 in 75 μL of FACS buffer.
Combine tube 13 (13-G1_1_CTV+) with tube 16 (16-G2_2_CTV-) for EXP 1.
Combine tube 14 (14-G1_2-CTV-) with tube 15 (15-G2_1-CTV+) for EXP 2.
Mix 1.5 µg of IgG to each tube.
Incubate tubes at 21°C–23°C for 10 minutes.
Add biotin anti-CD140, biotin anti-CD31, biotin anti-Ter-119, and biotin anti-CD45 to specified tubes.
Incubate tubes at 21°C–23°C for 20–30 minutes.
Add anti-EpCAM-APC to specified tubes.
Add anti-CD49f-PE/Cy7 to specified tubes.
Add anti-Sca1-FITC to specified tubes.
Add anti-CD49b-APC/Cy7 to specified tubes.
Add streptavidin-Brilliant Violet 570 to specified tubes.
Incubate tubes on wet ice for 20–30 minutes.
Add 1 ml FACS buffer to each tube and centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant carefully from each tube.
Resuspend each tube in 1 ml of FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant from each tube.
Resuspend tubes in 250–1,000 μl of FACS buffer.
Transfer contents to 5 ml round bottom polystyrene tubes.
Store tubes on wet ice in the dark until ready for sorter.
Analyze compensation controls (tubes 2–9) to select appropriate laser power and outputs for each of the dyes.
Use single stained samples from tubes 2, 3, 5–9 to correct for spectral overlap.
Add a tube containing a mix of stains from tubes 2 and 3 (tube 4) to compensate for the dump channel.
Adjust laser output and channel compensation settings according to the instrument used.
Re-run samples after making adjustments to ensure gates are correctly established.
Analyze FMO-Sca-1 (tube 10).
Use Forward Scatter-Area (FSC-A) versus Side Scatter Area (SSC-A) parameters for gating.
Select a cell population with uniform SSC-A across the range of FSC-A (p1).
Plot p1 on FSC-H/A to select single cells (p2).
Gated to remove dead cells (Zombie Yellow positive) and Lineage+ (Cd140a+, CD31+, Ter-119+, CD45+) cells.
Plot live cells on EpCam and CD49f to select the luminal population (EpCamhigh CD49fmedium).
Plot luminal cells from FMO controls on Sca-1/CD49b to determine 4-way gates.
Apply the gates from previous steps to tube 12.
Separate luminal cells into CTV+ and CTV- populations.
Reapply 4-way gates to CTV+ and CTV- cells for 4-way split.
Use FSC-Height (FSC-H) versus FSC-A to reject doublets and aggregates.
Select live Lineage- cells that are ZY- using FSC-A versus ZY+Lineage channel.
Identify luminal cells by selecting EpCAM versus CD49F, which are EpCAM(high)CD49f(med).
Obtain 0% of cells in the upper quadrants by analyzing Sca-1 versus CD49b with a four way gate.
Analyze FMO-CD49b and select Sca-1 versus CD49b with a four way gate to obtain 0% of cells in the right-side quadrants.
Consult with the FACS facility or operator regarding sorting parameters and available collection set-ups.
Sort cells on FACS Aria II at 30 psi using a 100 μm nozzle.
Maintain collected cells at 4°C during the sort.
Collect cells in 500 μL of collection media.
Replace collection tube with a new one containing 500 μL of collection media when volume reaches approximately 1 mL.
Spin down cells after sorting is complete.
Combine tubes containing the same populations.
